movement_source: row 'Return on equity – "cash basis" (%)', column 30 Jun 20 (full year) -> column 30 Jun 21 (full year)
headline: CBA's return on equity (cash basis, continuing operations) rose 130 basis points to 11.5% in FY21 from a restated 10.2% in FY20. The bank attributes the movement to "the impact of higher profit (approximately 200 basis points), partly offset by an increase in capital levels (approximately 70 basis points)". Applying the prescribed identity to disclosed figures: earnings_effect = 10.2% prior ROE x 19.8% cash NPAT growth (+$1,428m to $8,653m) = +2.0ppt at constant equity; equity_effect = 1.3 - 2.0 = -0.7ppt, as net average equity rose 6.1% (derived) to $75,187m on retained earnings (71% cash payout) and a 150bpts CET1 build to 13.1%. Both derived contributions are corroborated by the bank's own approximations. On a statutory basis ROE rose 140bpts (11.8% vs 10.4%); including discontinued operations, +120bpts (11.7% vs 10.5%). FY20 comparatives are restated: as originally reported, FY20 cash ROE was 10.3% (cash NPAT $7,296m), which would imply a ~120bpts movement. CBA's 11.5% led its peer set (11.1%, 10.2%, 9.7%) as at March 2021.

drivers.bank_label: Impact of higher profit (approximately 200 basis points)
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: prior ROE 10.2% x 19.8% cash NPAT growth (+$1,428m to $8,653m) = +2.02ppt at constant equity; bank states "approximately 200 basis points". Underpinned by $1,964m lower loan impairment expense - lower collective provision charges on improved economic conditions and outlook - plus 1.7% income growth, against 3.3% expense growth.

drivers.bank_label: Increase in capital levels (approximately 70 basis points)
drivers.narrative: Derived residual: +1.3ppt total minus +2.02ppt earnings = -0.72ppt; bank states "approximately 70 basis points". Net average equity rose 6.1% (derived) to $75,187m as the 71% cash payout left retained earnings and CET1 built 150bpts to 13.1%, above APRA's 10.5% benchmark; the $6.0bn buy-back was announced only at FY21 results and the interim DRP used on-market purchases.
Nil by construction: the prescribed identity assigns the interaction term to the equity effect, so no unmapped residual remains; the derived contributions sum exactly to the printed 130bpts movement.

notable_items: $6.0bn off-market share buy-back announced with the FY21 results: announced after the FY21 average-equity measurement period, so it did not affect FY21 ROE.
limitations: The earnings/equity split is derived from the prescribed identity, not a bank-disclosed bridge; the bank discloses only approximations (approximately 200bps profit, approximately 70bps capital).
The equity_effect includes the interaction term by construction of the identity, so the split is sequential, not simultaneous.
No primary ROE walk chart exists in the corpus (bank_language lists no roe_walk_labels for CBA); the decomposition rests on the KPI table, the narrative approximations and the derivation.

FY20 comparatives are restated; on originally reported FY20 figures (ROE 10.3%, cash NPAT $7,296m, net average equity $70,880m) the movement would be approximately 120bpts and the split would shift slightly.
The 6.1% growth in net average equity is derived from disclosed levels, not stated by the bank.

The bank does not disclose a reason for the increase in average equity beyond the capital and dividend facts cited; the retained-earnings/DRP/buy-back reasoning supporting the equity effect's direction is assembled from those disclosed facts.
Capped at 80: other_unmapped +0 ppt. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
